column42: Fun experiment! I thought the steering from the sketch generally worked OK for basic moodboarding, but I wouldn't consider it helpful for actual UI design. It would be interesting to use the results from the diffusion model to steer an autoregressive one. And just a note on the study design: the text glitches in the examples made it hard to judge whether a CTA / title was effectively represented, because most of the time the content from the prompt was just not present (or present in a very distorted form). In those situations I mostly counted the CTAs as not accurately represented.

A lot of these generated designs look visually like what you'd expect at first glance, but quickly fall apart upon closer inspection. I have seen better design prototypes from prompts that generate mockup UI's in code. Another approach to consider might be generating coded mockups and using a headless browser to screenshot the design.

It was really rewarding for me to contribute to your research. I genuinely see a lot of value in the proposal.

In a few moments, I chose answers that leaned away from “agree” because some simple instructions weren’t followed. For example, Asked for London and got beach images, or requested a search bar and it didn’t appear within an e-commerce context, which I find quite important.

Congratulations on the work!

column42: As a UX/UI designer, I think generative AI will bring drastic changes to how the typical designer workflow has been done in the past 10 years. That being said, I don't think it will replace designers' capacity for defining problems and how to solve them. I also believe hard work, iteration, and craft will still persist in AI-enhanced workflows. Although the tools are changing, along with the velocity and scope of what UX/UI design work is, matters of what makes a product great for users, as well as how to approach undefined problems and new challenges, remain very much human abilities.
